title: One Synapse, Turned Up or Down

scenes.tts: Can one synapse be turned up, and also turned down? In slices of rat hippocampus, it can. Give the Schaffer collateral input to C A one cells a fast train, one hundred pulses per second. It can leave a lasting increase. A long slow train of nine hundred pulses, at one to three hertz, can leave a lasting decrease. Same synapse, same transmitter. What tells the two apart?
scenes.caption: Can one synapse be turned up, and also turned down? In slices of rat hippocampus, it can. Give the Schaffer collateral input to CA1 cells a fast train, 100 pulses per second. scenes.visual: One synapse with a terminal and a spine; a fast train (dense ticks) grows a green bar, a slow train (sparse ticks) shrinks a red bar; a question mark lands in the spine.

scenes.tts: Look at one synapse. The Schaffer collateral terminal releases glutamate onto a spine of the C A one cell. Two kinds of receptor listen. AMPA receptors carry most of the ordinary response. N M D A receptors sit beside them. At resting potential, a magnesium ion sits in their pore. Glutamate binds, but the pore stays plugged.
scenes.caption: Look at one synapse. The Schaffer collateral terminal releases glutamate onto a spine of the CA1 cell. Two kinds of receptor listen. AMPA receptors carry most of the ordinary response. NMDA receptors sit beside them. At resting potential, a magnesium ion sits in their pore. Glutamate binds, but the pore stays plugged.
scenes.visual: Glutamate leaves the terminal; the view zooms to the membrane; AMPA and NMDA receptors are named; magnesium plugs the NMDA pores and stays.
scenes.narration: Look at one synapse. The Schaffer collateral terminal releases glutamate onto a spine of the CA1 cell. Two kinds of receptor listen. scenes.tts: Now depolarize the cell while glutamate is bound. The magnesium is driven out of the pore. The N M D A receptor then passes sodium, potassium and calcium. It needs glutamate, a co-agonist and depolarization together, so it works as a coincidence detector. In rat slices, the blocker A P V leaves the ordinary response alone. A high frequency train then fails to produce L T P.
scenes.caption: Now depolarize the cell while glutamate is bound. The magnesium is driven out of the pore. The NMDA receptor then passes sodium, potassium and calcium. It needs glutamate, a co-agonist and depolarization together, so it works as a coincidence detector. In rat slices, the blocker APV leaves the ordinary response alone. A high frequency train then fails to produce LTP.
scenes.visual: The membrane turns to depolarized, the plugs leave the pores, calcium flows in; two conditions add up to an open receptor; APV caps the NMDA receptors.

scenes.tts: A large rise of calcium in the spine is the trigger for L T P. In the canonical model, it recruits C a M K two, a kinase that can stay active after calcium falls. Expression includes more AMPA receptors at the synapse. The same test pulse now gives a bigger response.
scenes.caption: A large rise of calcium in the spine is the trigger for LTP. In the canonical model, it recruits CaMKII, a kinase that can stay active after calcium falls. Expression includes more AMPA receptors at the synapse. The same test pulse now gives a bigger response.
scenes.visual: A large calcium rise fills the spine, CaMKII appears and stays after calcium fades, new AMPA receptors join the membrane, a green response bar rises.
scenes.narration: A large rise of calcium in the spine is the trigger for LTP. In the canonical model, it recruits CaMKII, a kinase that can stay active after calcium falls. Expression includes more AMPA receptors at the synapse. The same test pulse now gives a bigger response.

scenes.tts: Now the slow train. It gives a modest, prolonged rise of calcium. In the canonical model, that preferentially recruits protein phosphatases, rather than C a M K two. Expression includes removing AMPA receptors by endocytosis. The same test pulse now gives a smaller response, only at the conditioned input.
scenes.caption: Now the slow train. It gives a modest, prolonged rise of calcium. In the canonical model, that preferentially recruits protein phosphatases, rather than CaMKII. scenes.visual: A trickle of calcium, phosphatases appear, two AMPA receptors are pulled into the spine, the conditioned input's bar falls while the other input's bar stays.
scenes.narration: Now the slow train. It gives a modest, prolonged rise of calcium. In the canonical model, that preferentially recruits protein phosphatases, rather than CaMKII. scenes.tts: In the model, a dimmer switch with one input wire. How much calcium comes through decides the direction. But that calcium rule is a model. No single calcium threshold between L T D and L T P is established. And L T P is a family. Mossy fibre L T P in guinea pig C A three does not need the N M D A receptor. The same synapse turns up or down with its pattern of activity.
